$comment: THE docs contract. Single source of truth for the documentation system.
Every other artefact — AGENTS.md, the docs-updater runbook, the how-to recipes,
and scripts/docs-check.mjs — reads this file rather than hardcoding paths,
commands, or subject layout. If reality disagrees with this file, fix this file
and say why. Do not work around it in a consumer.
Subject IDs are stable: once assigned, never reused, never renumbered. Folder
names may be renamed ONLY together with an edit to this file.

repo.commitCountNote: Five commits, the last two landing the overlay-delivery and event-query stages. The daily-summary, web-dashboard, and demo phases are uncommitted — see repo shape in 03-repository/01-current-state.md. Git is read-only to agents; the human owns every commit.

packageManager.name: npm
evidence: ARCHITECTURE.md §9.1 specifies `npm install` as the install step, so npm is the
specification's own choice, not an inference. npm 10.9+/12 resolves workspaces
natively, so the planned firetv/ and web/ packages need no extra tooling.

changedFrom.previous: detected: false — no manifest and no lockfile existed
changedFrom.reason: The tooling phase created package.json and ran npm install. The contract is updated to match reality rather than the plan being worked around.

workspaces.note: ARCHITECTURE.md §11 plans a second package.json in firetv/ and another in web/. Workspaces are NOT declared yet because npm fails on workspace globs that match nothing. Add "workspaces": ["firetv", "web"] to package.json in the same change that creates those directories.

runtimes.declaredByRepoNote: The repository declares no runtime. The two spec documents describe a planned TypeScript/AWS SAM system that does not exist yet.

docsCheckRuntime.name: node
docsCheckRuntime.justification: scripts/docs-check.mjs is dependency-free plain Node ES modules using only node: built-ins, so it runs on a clean checkout with no install step. The repository has no manifest and no toolchain to compile a TypeScript variant, so a .ts validator could not be run today. Rename to .ts once a package manager and build tool exist.

buildTools.name: AWS SAM
buildTools.note: ARCHITECTURE.md §8.3 plans `sam build && sam deploy --guided`. template.yaml now exists and declares 25 resources, including seven AWS::Serverless::Function resources across five source files — webhookHandler.handler, snapshotFetcher.handler, overlayPusher.handler, overlayPusher.onConnect, overlayPusher.onDisconnect, eventQuery.handler, and dailySummary.handler. Two of the 25 are conditional on CostAlarmEmail being non-empty. None of the task-runner files above exists, and no samconfig.toml does. The SAM CLI itself is still unavailable — see commands.dev — so the template has never been built or deployed.

changedFrom.previous: detected: false — no template.yaml and no task runner
changedFrom.reason: The webhook-ingress and overlay-delivery phases created template.yaml. The contract is updated to match reality rather than the plan being worked around.

dev.reason: ARCHITECTURE.md §9.1 plans `sam local start-api`, and both template.yaml and the handlers now exist, so the missing piece is the SAM CLI itself rather than the code it would serve. Installing the SAM CLI would make this available; the contract has not been changed to assume that.

build.note: node scripts/build-lambda.mjs. esbuild bundles every file in src/handlers/ into a self-contained CommonJS file in dist/, preserving the src/handlers/ path that template.yaml's Handler property expects. Bundling rather than tsc emit is required because the AWS SDK v3 is not in the Lambda runtime, so a dist/ of loose files would deploy a handler that cannot require its own dependencies.

buildWeb.note: node scripts/build-web.mjs. esbuild bundles web/src/ into web/dist/app.js as an ES module for the browser, and copies index.html and app.css beside it. platform: browser, not node, is the line that matters: under platform: node esbuild would leave a require() a browser cannot execute. The dashboard has no dependencies to inline, so this is not a bundling-for-deployment problem like commands.build — it exists to give the browser one module URL instead of four and to fail loudly on a parse error. Its output is NOT checked by commands.buildVerify, which asserts the Lambda bundles in dist/.

buildFiretv.note: node scripts/build-firetv.mjs. esbuild bundles firetv/src/ into firetv/dist/overlay.js as an ES module for the WebView that hosts the overlay, and copies overlay.html and overlay.css beside it. platform: browser, for the same reason as buildWeb. It reads firetv/src/ and writes firetv/dist/, so it cannot fail on ordering; it is in CI and in commands.all for parity rather than because anything asserts on its output. There is no verify-bundle equivalent: the overlay has no dependencies to inline and its output is not a Lambda.

test.note: vitest run, discovering test/**/*.test.ts via vitest.config.ts.

testCoverage.metricNote: The first real single-number metric this repository has had, and therefore the first thing an optimisation loop could measure. The current figure is reported in docs/03-repository/03-verification-commands.md, which is where the number is re-read from coverage/coverage-summary.json after every run; this note deliberately does not duplicate it, because a stale percentage in the contract is worse than none. The uncovered remainder is dominated by default AWS-client construction in snapshotStore and connectionStore, which needs an AWS account to exercise, plus the SQS and schedule handler adapters. Those are recorded per module rather than left as a vague gap.

typecheck.note: tsc --noEmit in strict mode, covering test/ as well as src/, then two more passes over the browser surfaces, web/ and firetv/, each with a DOM lib. Three invocations because the repository targets three runtimes: the Lambda code is Node (types: [node], no DOM) and the dashboard and overlay client are browsers (DOM, no Node types). Sharing one config would let each side typecheck against the other's globals. Browser test files are typechecked on their own side, so mocks must match the real signatures. typecheck:web and typecheck:firetv exist so the second and third passes can be run on their own.

lint.reason: No linter installed and no lint config. Deliberately not added in the tooling phase: a linter is a second opinion on style, not a correctness gate, and typecheck already fails the build on type errors. Add one when style drift becomes a real problem, and update this block then.

buildVerify.note: node scripts/verify-bundle.mjs. Asserts no bundled file requires a package it did not inline. This catches the deployment failure that nothing else reports: tsc emit shipping bare require('@aws-sdk/...') calls, where the Lambda starts and only fails on the first invocation.

all.run: npm run typecheck && npm test && npm run build && npm run build:verify && npm run build:web && npm run build:firetv && npm run docs:check
all.note: Every gate in one command. Wired as the single local pre-commit substitute and used by the author to close each phase. commands.build appears before buildVerify: the gate asserts against dist/, and until 2026-10-04 `all` assumed dist/ already existed — which made it fail on a clean checkout and let a stale dist/ pass the gate against changed source. Building first fixed both, and made `all` step-for-step identical to CI. buildFiretv sits beside buildWeb: order-independent, in the chain for parity with CI. See ci.workflows[0].note.

paths.sourceRootsNote: Populated by the tooling phase. src/ is the product code, test/ holds the vitest suites, scripts/ holds the documentation validator. Rule 3 in AGENTS.md keys off this list.
paths.routeGlobsNote: Populated by the overlay-delivery phase. overlayPusher.ts exports the WebSocket $connect and $disconnect routes alongside the SQS consumer, so route globs now cover route handlers as well as consumers. Both were previously empty, and an empty glob would have let a route land undocumented. The glob is identical to handlerGlobs because every route lives in a handler file; they are kept as two keys because they answer different questions and a future route may live elsewhere.
paths.handlerGlobsNote: Active as of the webhook-ingress phase. src/handlers/ now exists, so a handler that no document references fails the validator. A handler can no longer land undocumented.
paths.libGlobsNote: Reverse coverage for shared library modules. Active as of the tooling phase, so a module under src/lib/ that no document mentions now fails the validator. This is what makes reverse coverage APPLICABLE for the first time. Note that this glob is anchored at the repository root: web/src/api.ts matches NEITHER this nor handlerGlobs, so the dashboard has no reverse coverage at all. See limitations.
paths.webGlobsNote: Intentionally empty. Populated by the web-dashboard phase only if webGlobs is filled in with web/src/**/*.ts, and that is blocked on a real problem: check 5's globs are also read by nothing else, but a web module imported by a test under test/ fails to resolve under the root Node tsconfig, so reverse coverage for web/ needs the test tree moved first. The dashboard is documented by hand in docs/07-web-dashboard/ instead, and check 5's blind spot for it is recorded in limitations.
paths.excludeGlobsNote: Active. Fixtures and generated output are excluded from reverse coverage because they are inputs, not surface. *.test.* and *.spec.* are excluded so a test file does not count as documentation of the module it exercises. Migrations are excluded by default; flip this if the project later wants migrations documented individually.

pathVerification.$comment: Drives check 1. Decides which backticked tokens in docs are assertions about real files.
pathVerification.basenameFallbackNote: A bare filename with no slash, e.g. 00-overview.md, is satisfied by any file of that name in the repo. This lets docs cite a filename pattern without pinning one subject folder.
pathVerification.secretsAlsoScanNote: Secret and absolute-path scanning is wider than path-existence scanning. The two spec documents are inputs, not documentation, so path assertions in them are not this system's business — but a pasted credential in them still is. Their .env.example block is placeholder-valued, so it does not trip the generic check.

markers.expectAbsentNote: A self-invalidating declaration that a named path does not exist yet. Check 1 fails the declaration itself once the file is created, so a blind spot cannot rot. A live skipPlanned region is exempt from validation but every path inside it is printed in the run summary.

provenance.$comment: Drives check 8. Every sub-file must declare what it was verified against.
provenance.rule: State the file and section, and where possible the symbol. If a claim rests on a specification rather than on code, say so explicitly and mark it unverified against code. Never imply a symbol exists when no code exists.

secrets.$comment: Drives check 6. High-confidence provider token shapes plus generic credential assignments.

genericAssignment.$comment: The leading (?<![A-Za-z0-9]) instead of \b is deliberate: \b does not fire between _ and C because both are word characters, so prefixed forms like RING_CLIENT_SECRET= were missed entirely.
genericAssignment.mixedEntropyRule: The captured value must contain at least one uppercase, one lowercase, and one digit, and be at least 16 characters, and must not match a placeholder hint.

absolutePathPrefixes.$comment: Drives check 7. Absolute local filesystem paths leak a developer's machine into shared docs.

subjectsNote: Order is reading priority, not creation order. Numbers are NN prefixes on folder names and must match the order value. The validator fails if a docs/NN-* folder has no entry here, or if an entry here has no folder, or if NN disagrees with order. That is what makes silent renumbering impossible. Orders are also unique: two subjects cannot share a number, so a new subject always takes the next unused one rather than an attractive lower one.

reverseCoverage.intentionallyUndocumentedNote: Entries are { path, reason }. A matching file is exempted from reverse coverage with the reason printed in the run summary. Keep this list empty unless a file genuinely should not be described.

agent.docsUpdaterNote: The canonical docs-sync runbook. Single source of truth for the process. Human-readable mirror is docs/00-how-to/04-run-a-docs-sync-pass.md. If one changes, change both.

docsIndexesNote: Every subject folder must be reachable from each of these, by literal path or by a link that resolves into it. This is what stops a subject from being declared in the contract and in the docs tree while being invisible to the agent that reads the router first.

ci.detectedFrom: origin remote is github.com; .github/workflows/ is the only workflow directory

workflows.note: One job runs all five available gates, in the order `npm run all` chains them: typecheck, test, build, build:verify, build:web, build:firetv, and docs:check. build:verify was closed into CI on 2026-10-04 after being recorded as a gap: the gate is order-dependent — scripts/verify-bundle.mjs asserts against dist/, which only exists after commands.build runs — so closing it meant adding the build step before it, not the gate alone. The workflow had previously carried the gate in its documented step list without a build step to feed it, which is the failure Friction Log Entry 14 describes. build:web and build:firetv stay last-but-two for the same reason they were always safe: each reads one source tree and writes its own dist/, so no ordering can break them. Note that their outputs, web/dist/ and firetv/dist/, are not gitignored, so CI writes them and discards them — that is deliberate, since both surfaces deploy as static files rather than from this repository.

Publishes the two demo pages to GitHub Pages on every push to main: web/dist/ under /dashboard/, firetv/dist/ under /overlay/, and scripts/demo-landing.html as the site root. Reads its build commands from the contract exactly like the checks workflow, per Entry 14's own suggestion. It runs no gates — checks runs them — and requires a one-time manual enable: repo settings, Pages, Source = GitHub Actions. Until that enable happens and the human pushes, the published URL does not exist; do not cite a Pages URL as live before both. Added 2026-10-04 as the durable hosting path for the demos (decision D035).

gitHooks.status: No hook system of any kind. .git/hooks exists but is empty; core.hooksPath is unset.
gitHooks.advisoryWarning: Skipped deliberately. The prompt conditions the advisory drift warning on an existing hook system, and none exists. Introducing husky, lefthook, or a pre-commit framework purely to carry a warning would change the repository's hook posture without being asked. When a hook system appears, prepend a warning that prints the validator output and never alters the existing exit code.

limitations: This contract records discovered reality as of 2026-09-28. It is a description, not an enforcement of the build.

docs-check proves document structure, not truth. It cannot confirm that a documented auth requirement, status code, parameter, or behaviour actually matches the handler, because it does not read semantics. A passing docs:check is never evidence that the docs are correct.

Device names are now resolved, but never observed. src/lib/ringClient.getDevice() is called by the describe stage since decision D031, and it has still never made a real Ring request: the response shape is verified against documentation, not traffic. Nothing depends on the name being correct — a failed lookup costs the event its name and nothing else.

web/ has NO reverse coverage. paths.libGlobs and paths.handlerGlobs are src/** only, so a new file under web/src/ will not fail the validator if the documentation stops naming it. The dashboard is currently documented by hand in docs/07-web-dashboard/01-dashboard.md. Widening the globs is blocked on a second problem: the root tsconfig is Node-only and the dashboard is browser-only, so a web module imported by a suite under test/ cannot resolve. Both trees are kept separate on purpose (decision D029); the globs should follow, not lead.

firetv/ has the same NO-reverse-coverage gap as web/, for the same reason: it is a third typechecking tree (Node root, two browser surfaces), documented by hand in docs/08-fire-tv-overlay/. Three trees now share the pattern: the root tsconfig is Node-only, and each browser surface carries its own DOM tsconfig and its own copy of the small fake DOM.

The dashboard is not React. ARCHITECTURE.md §11 sketches web/src/App.tsx and components/EventTimeline.tsx. What exists is four TypeScript files with no dependencies, because npm install hangs in this environment and react cannot be fetched. Recorded as decision D029, along with the loss that implies: no JSX, no component structure. The layer split means a later swap touches only app.ts, main.ts, and the build.

No npm workspaces field is declared even though web/package.json now exists, because CI runs npm ci and a lockfile that does not record the new workspace fails outright rather than repairing itself. Regenerating the lockfile needs an install, which does not work here. Recorded as decision D030. Cost today is nil: web/package.json declares no dependencies.

Reverse coverage is ACTIVE for src/lib, src/handlers, and route handlers. A new file in any of them that no document names fails the validator. This proved its worth in the query phase: creating src/handlers/eventQuery.ts failed check 1 in five documents at once, because five separate expect-absent declarations had listed it. That is the mechanism working, not a nuisance.

GET /events/today required an auth mechanism that ARCHITECTURE.md does not specify. A static X-Query-Key was added, fails closed when unset, and is recorded as decision D022. There is still no per-account separation: one table, one key, one homeowner. Not deployable for a real multi-user product.

GET /events/today returns an extra `summary` field that ARCHITECTURE.md §5.2 does not specify, because §3.6 writes the daily summary into the same partition and nothing else would read it. The field is additive and `null` before the schedule runs. The dashboard renders it, including the fallback-source label, and did so in a real browser on 2026-10-04 — but never against a deployed backend.

The events table is partitioned by a UTC date (D014) and GET /events/today defaults to that partition, overridable with ?date=. A homeowner's local day is not computed anywhere; the dashboard exposes the ?date= override as a date input, which is as far as local time is handled.

template.yaml has never been deployed or validated. No AWS account and no SAM CLI are available, so it is checked only for YAML well-formedness and for consistency with the build output. Every Handler path is asserted to match a real file in dist/, and that is as far as verification goes.

Nothing in src/lib/ringClient.ts or src/lib/bedrockClient.ts has been exercised against live AWS or Ring. There is no webhook or media simulator; the Developer Playground issues tokens and simulates live view only. Every request shape is verified against documentation, not observed traffic.

The Bedrock request envelope is the least-verified thing in the repository: no AWS documentation was fetched while writing it. It fails loudly, as an API error caught into the FR11 fallback, rather than silently.

The trigger for EncryptedMediaError is an inference, not a documented fact: Ring states TAKE/E2EE media comes back encrypted but publishes no status code or content type for it. Recorded as decision D016.

The picture-in-picture overlay specified in ARCHITECTURE.md 3.4 is NOT implemented, because no documented Vega OS API supports it. The delivery half is implemented, and since D034 the client side is too — on the WebView surface Vega does sanction — but FR12, appearing over another app's playback, remains a platform limit. Recorded as decision D021.

ARCHITECTURE.md §6 asks for a CloudWatch billing alarm against Bedrock cost runaway. An AWS Budget filtered to the Bedrock service is declared instead, because EstimatedCharges must be enabled per account from the Billing console and a template cannot do that. Recorded as decision D027. The budget has never been created and no notification has ever been sent.

Event and summary rows now write the 90-day expires_at that ARCHITECTURE.md §3.5 specifies, measured from the row's own date partition rather than from write time so a retry cannot extend retention. DynamoDB's documented 48-hour deletion lag has not been observed. Recorded as decision D028.

The daily summary is scheduled in a timezone parameter but reads a UTC date partition, so a zone behind UTC fires after that partition has begun. The default is UTC, where the two agree. Recorded as decision D025.

The §3.6 summary prompt is the specified text plus three appended clauses, and the stage uses 400 max tokens rather than §3.3's 80. Both are deviations from the specification, recorded as decision D026.

§3.6's optional SES email is not implemented. It needs a verified identity, a destination address, and an unsubscribe path, none of which the specification names. The summary is readable through GET /events/today instead.
FR6's 8-second end-to-end target is unmeasured and at risk: the path is three queue hops and the Bedrock call alone is several seconds. FR4's 5-second snapshot target is likewise unmeasured.
